selectionBoundary: Primary standards and official registries define cryptographic transport, append-only evidence, protected claim labels, and threat boundaries. They do not solve physical event accuracy, role independence, or causal identifiability. RC50 tests that application-layer boundary rather than proposing a new signature, Merkle tree, or transparency architecture.

sources.title: RFC 8949: Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR)
sources.usedFor: Core deterministic encoding, preferred shortest encodings, map-key ordering, and the distinction among well-formed, valid, and application-expected input.
sources.doesNotEstablish: COSE signature validity, receipt semantics, or physical accuracy.

sources.title: RFC 9052: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE): Structures and Process
sources.usedFor: COSE_Sign1, tag 18, protected versus unprotected headers, Sig_structure, detached payload, and empty external_aad in the frozen profile.
sources.doesNotEstablish: Application replay protection, transparency, or statement truth.

sources.title: RFC 9338: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE): Countersignatures
sources.usedFor: The prior-art boundary that a second party can separately sign a COSE object and that the resulting security meaning must be specified.
sources.doesNotEstablish: That two keys are operationally independent or that countersignature validation makes a nonce one-time. RC50 uses two separate Signed Statements and claims no header-11 conformance.

sources.title: RFC 9162: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
sources.usedFor: SHA-256 Merkle leaf/node domain separation, inclusion and consistency proof algorithms, retained signed tree heads, and the need to share log responses to detect inconsistent views.
sources.doesNotEstablish: Which conflicting branch is physically correct or that an entry's payload is accurate.

sources.title: RFC 9596: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) "typ" (type) Header Parameter
sources.usedFor: Protected COSE header label 16 identifying Signed Statement and Receipt media types before application processing.
sources.doesNotEstablish: That an application payload is accurate or that a message is fresh.

sources.title: RFC 9597: CBOR Web Token (CWT) Claims in COSE Headers
sources.usedFor: Protected COSE header label 15 carrying issuer and subject CWT claims required by the RC50 SCITT subset.
sources.doesNotEstablish: Uniqueness or accuracy of application sequence values.

sources.title: RFC 9942: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts
sources.usedFor: COSE receipt labels 394-396, VDS identifier RFC9162_SHA256=1, inclusion proof -1, consistency proof -2, detached-root verification order, and one joint receipt result.
sources.doesNotEstablish: Registration policy, physical event identity, role independence, currentness across observers, or truth of the logged statement.

sources.title: RFC 9943: An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains
sources.usedFor: Mandatory issuer/subject claims, Signed and Transparent Statement structures, multiple independent receipts, append-only/non-equivocation/replayability requirements, transparent registration policy, and the threat boundary between authentic statements and accurate claims.
sources.doesNotEstablish: That an issuer statement is true, that VDS order equals issuance order, or that a single transparency service exposes every conflicting view.

sources.title: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Registries
sources.usedFor: Current labels 1, 3, 4, 15, 16, 394, 395, 396; EdDSA -8; RFC9162_SHA256 VDS 1; and inclusion/consistency proof identifiers.

repositoryInheritance.notRepeated: RC50 does not rerun the 80 single-fault trials, refit X16 images, or claim another single-fault result.

repositoryInheritance.reused: Transactional one-time state, adversarial schedules, refusal under missing independent evidence, and explicit common-cause residuals.
repositoryInheritance.notRepeated: RC50 does not claim a new distributed-consensus or hardware-in-the-loop result.

repositoryInheritance.asset: RC31-RC34 attestation, role separation, transparency, and independent-verifier cycles
repositoryInheritance.reused: Protected identities, negative cryptographic controls, code-independent wire adjudication, and append-only receipt auditing.
repositoryInheritance.notRepeated: RC50 tests a published RFC 9942/9943 subset and composite physical-history claims rather than relabeling earlier JSON attestations.

stateReview.rfc9942: Published June 2026 as an Internet Standards Track document; it defines RFC9162_SHA256 inclusion and consistency receipt encodings.
stateReview.rfc9943: Published June 2026 as an Internet Standards Track document; it requires SCITT Signed Statements and Receipts to carry protected issuer and subject claims and explicitly separates registration from claim accuracy.
stateReview.iana: The official COSE registry was reviewed after both RFCs and lists receipt, VDS, and VDP labels 394-396 as of 2026-08-11.
stateReview.implementationBoundary: The official standards supply structures and algorithms but not the RC50 application policy, reset registry, physical witness definition, or causal candidate-history adjudicator.
